metadata.title: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.111

context:
## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Stefan Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.111
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.111
- Datum: 04.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 3 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hannah and Manfred, we are forwarding today the photos of
your daughter, lets hope, they will safely arrive. You will see
- they are excellent - that Eva is looking well and so your mothers
heart will be glad. Today she goes back to Accily Hall and I think
it is a good sign that she is rather eager to see her auntie Olga
again; she feels there perfectly at home and in all those good days
with her we heard not a single complaint about anything there. So we
are rather satisfied to have found the right thing. She ~~do~~ has made
some progress and I hope you will not regret that she has seen and
learned so much.
Thanks for all what you are doing for me. The consul has promis-
sed to me that a new power of attorney will be made in the Consu-
late here; I shall go there in the next few days. Please drop a
line also to Siegmund Warburg, and telling him that I have written
three times to him and once to Koerner and never got a reply. It
is really not my fault. And give Frietental all material help, I hope
I can send also to him a food-parcel.
We lose here much time by thinking what to do next. On the 15th
of May I shall have to speak at the great dinner of the Pen Club
one of this enormous dinners with 1000 persons which I have avoided
all my life long. But this time I cannot refuse as it is important
for our common cause. Somerset Maugham will speak - every one ten
minutes sharp - for the English, Sigrid Undset for the Scandinavian, Jules
Romains for the French and I for the German-speaking writers, the other
~~persons~~ {ones} get only 1 minute; I have to speak one half in German, the
other in English. All this will be relayed by short-wave all over the
world and I shall give you in time the exact hour, that you may hear
me in London. Will we have afterwards still time and occasion to
go to Brazil? Who can tell it? Lotte is now in competent treatment
and many tests are made to find out the real reason and center of her
asthma. I would not like to travel before she is perfectly fit. Love Stefan

[Rand links, vertikal:] I have written an obituary for our good Hermann Meine for
the "Anfanger" here and shall send it to his widow.

[Rand rechts, vertikal:] Best love (I will write soon)
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief von Stefan Zweig in violetter Tinte. Der Text am linken Rand ist vertikal geschrieben, ebenso der Text am rechten Rand.
Farbskala und Grauskala für Archivierung. Der Brief ist hinter die Skalen gelegt, der Text ist durch die Skalen teilweise verdeckt.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der handschriftlichen Natur und der Korrekturen. Die wenigen Korrekturen (durchgestrichene Wörter, eingefügte Wörter) wurden gemäß den Anweisungen transkribiert.
